idiom_name: enum with associated values + exhaustive switch over a command stream or actor mailbox
implementation_notes: Swift expresses the command as an enum with associated values - one case per operation carrying its parameters - and dispatch is a switch that the compiler checks for exhaustiveness, which replaces the command class and protocol hierarchy for a closed operation set. Payloads that cross a process or network boundary conform to Codable and are encoded with JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder, while the carrier is an AsyncStream, a Combine publisher or an actor whose mailbox serializes execution. A protocol with existential values (any Command) is the fallback when other modules must add operations.
pitfalls: The compiler-synthesized Codable form for enums with associated values has changed across Swift versions and is not a stable cross-platform wire format; pin an explicit encoding when another language or runtime decodes the command.
An actor's mailbox serializes commands but does not persist them: a command sent while the actor is being replaced is dropped, so cross-process commands need a durable channel.
Making the command protocol-existential (any Command) loses exhaustive checking and the value-type copy semantics; keep the enum closed unless extension by other modules is a real requirement.
